world_news.headline: Stokes returns to England captaincy for third Test against New Zealand
world_news.summary: Captain Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson have returned to England's squad for the third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge following the conclusion of a disciplinary hearing.

world_news.headline: Australia posts seven-wicket T20I win over Bangladesh as Spencer Johnson stars with ball
world_news.summary: Spencer Johnson proves to be a menace with the ball for Australia, as the tourists complete a T20I series clean sweep against Bangladesh.

world_news.headline: Mourners gather to remember Lebanese conservationist killed by Israel
world_news.summary: People gathered in Beirut in memory of beloved turtle conservationist Mona Khalil, killed in Israeli attack.

world_news.headline: Remembering Al Jazeera cameraman Ahmed Wishah’s life’s work
world_news.summary: Al Jazeera cameraman Ahmed Wishah dedicated his life to documenting life in Gaza before he was killed by Israel.

world_news.headline: Serena Williams to play women’s singles at Wimbledon as wildcard entrant
world_news.summary: The seven-time ladies' singles champion will make her Grand Slam return at Wimbledon, six years after her last appearance.

world_news.headline: Displaced Lebanese inspect shattered Nabatieh after Israel halts attacks
world_news.summary: Displaced residents returned to Nabatieh after Israel ordered a halt to fighting in southern Lebanon.

world_news.headline: Colombia elections take place as Abelardo de la Espriella leads polls
world_news.summary: Colombians are voting in an election where senator Ivan Cepeda is racing against Abelardo de la Espriella.

world_news.headline: Japan fans celebrate 4-0 World Cup win in Tokyo
world_news.summary: Fans gathered at Tokyo's Shibuya Crossing after Japan beat Tunisia 4-0 in a World Cup group-stage match.

world_news.headline: Ramiro Valdes, one of Cuba’s last living revolutionary figures, dies at 94
world_news.summary: Valdes was close ally of Castro brothers and helped found Cuba's notorious intelligence apparatus.

world_news.headline: How Australia's World Cup chef knows the players like his food
world_news.summary: Chef Vini Capovilla has learnt a thing or two catering for the Socceroos at four World Cups. And one is finding out if they like his food.
